key_battle: QB Efficiency: DAL has the clearest edge over CLE — score 10.0/10.

football_factors.name: QB Efficiency
football_factors.reason: DAL's QB efficiency is significantly higher than CLE's this season (0.370 EPA/play difference) — a gap that shapes drive consistency and big-play rate.

football_factors.name: Turnover Edge
football_factors.reason: DAL wins the turnover battle modestly — a 0.77 turnover-per-game edge that creates shorter fields and extra possessions.

football_factors.name: Offensive Efficiency
football_factors.reason: DAL's offense generates significantly more expected points per play than CLE's (0.217 EPA/play difference), keeping drives alive and converting more consistently.

football_factors.name: Defensive Resistance
football_factors.reason: DAL's defense is slightly more stingy than CLE's — allowing 0.028 fewer EPA per play and limiting opponent scoring opportunities.

football_factors.name: Pressure Matchup
football_factors.reason: DAL wins the pass rush vs. protection battle slightly (0.009 sack-rate edge) — a mismatch that can collapse key third-down drives.

explanation: Clark gives the slight edge to CLE at 52%. CLE pressure the quarterback on 11% of dropbacks; per-play EPA allowed is otherwise close. The one thing that could turn it: DAL are the team trending up. Last three: DAL 2-1, CLE 1-2 (15 pt/gm margin swing).

football_factors.name: QB Efficiency
football_factors.reason: IND's QB efficiency is slightly higher than HOU's this season (0.018 EPA/play difference) — a gap that shapes drive consistency and big-play rate.

football_factors.name: Turnover Edge

football_factors.name: Offensive Efficiency

football_factors.name: Defensive Resistance

explanation: Clark leans HOU at 60%. Last three: HOU 2-1, IND 1-2 (10 pt/gm margin swing). The one thing that could turn it: IND bring the pass rush that matters here. IND pressure the quarterback on 25% of dropbacks; per-play EPA allowed is otherwise close.

key_battle: QB Efficiency: IND has the clearest edge over TEN — score 8.2/10.

football_factors.name: QB Efficiency

football_factors.name: Offensive Efficiency

football_factors.name: Defensive Resistance

factor_cards.explanation: It's a division game, so both staffs know each other cold; expect a grindier, tighter margin than the raw numbers suggest. 15 mph wind: Moderate wind (11–20 mph): minimal impact; deep routes may be affected. Game-time temperature is around 50°F.
factor_cards.baseline_note: DET 0d rest · divisional · 50°F · 15 mph wind

factor_cards.name: Recent Offense
factor_cards.headline: Recent offense is close to even.
factor_cards.explanation: This is the model's thinnest read: on a per-play basis GB and DET have been about even on offense over the last three weeks. GB's offense has still been elite in absolute terms, so this isn't a weakness — it's just not where the edge in this matchup comes from.
factor_cards.baseline_note: GB's offense is producing +0.14 EPA/play over its last three — elite vs the rest of the league.

factor_cards.name: Defensive Edge
factor_cards.headline: GB's defense has been the tougher unit.
factor_cards.explanation: GB's defense has been the sturdier of the two, giving up 0.05 fewer EPA/play than DET on the season. A lot of it is pressure — GB are getting to the quarterback on 13% of dropbacks, the kind of heat that rattles J.Goff. If they keep J.Goff uncomfortable, DET's scoring drives are the ones that stall out.
factor_cards.baseline_note: GB allow 0.05 fewer EPA/play than DET on the season, pressure on 13% of dropbacks.

factor_cards.name: Momentum
factor_cards.headline: Records level, but GB hit harder.
factor_cards.explanation: Both teams are 3-0 over their last three, so the win-loss trend is a wash. The tiebreaker is scoring margin — GB hold roughly 17 points per game of margin separation their way. Form like that tends to carry: healthier rotations, cleaner execution, and more belief in the tight moments.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Last three: both 3-0; GB +17 pt/gm scoring margin.

factor_cards.name: Market Edge
factor_cards.headline: Vegas gives Even the slight nod.
factor_cards.explanation: Here Clark is taking the other side of the market — Vegas actually made DET a 2.5-point favorite — about a 61% implied win probability. That disagreement is the interesting part: the model sees something in the football matchup the line is underrating.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Market line: DET a 2.5-point favorite.

factor_cards.headline: WAS's offense is heating up.
factor_cards.explanation: Over the last three weeks WAS have been the more efficient offense — averaging +0.16 EPA/play more than PHI and staying on schedule +9% more often. That production is elite by league standards this season. And the gap has grown over the last few weeks, not shrunk. Against PHI, expect WAS to move the ball more consistently and lean on that efficiency on early downs.
factor_cards.baseline_note: WAS's offense is producing +0.18 EPA/play over its last three — elite vs the rest of the league.

factor_cards.name: Defensive Edge
factor_cards.headline: WAS bring the pass rush that matters here.
factor_cards.explanation: The two defenses have been close on a per-play basis, so WAS's edge is about disruption: they're getting to the quarterback on 10% of dropbacks. That pressure is what tilts the matchup — keeping J.Hurts uncomfortable is how PHI's scoring drives stall out.
factor_cards.baseline_note: WAS pressure the quarterback on 10% of dropbacks; per-play EPA allowed is otherwise close.

factor_cards.name: Momentum
factor_cards.headline: Records level, but PHI hit harder.
factor_cards.explanation: Both teams are 3-0 over their last three, so the win-loss trend is a wash. The tiebreaker is scoring margin — PHI hold roughly 1 point per game of margin separation their way. Form like that tends to carry: healthier rotations, cleaner execution, and more belief in the tight moments.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Last three: both 3-0; PHI +1 pt/gm scoring margin.

factor_cards.name: Market Edge
factor_cards.headline: The market leans Even.
factor_cards.explanation: Here Clark is taking the other side of the market — Vegas actually made PHI a 6.0-point favorite — about a 33% implied win probability. That disagreement is the interesting part: the model sees something in the football matchup the line is underrating.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Market line: PHI a 6.0-point favorite.

football_factors.name: QB Efficiency
football_factors.reason: PHI's QB efficiency is meaningfully higher than KC's this season (0.196 EPA/play difference) — a gap that shapes drive consistency and big-play rate.

football_factors.name: Turnover Edge
football_factors.reason: PHI wins the turnover battle modestly — a 0.72 turnover-per-game edge that creates shorter fields and extra possessions.

football_factors.name: Offensive Efficiency
football_factors.reason: PHI's offense generates modestly more expected points per play than KC's (0.090 EPA/play difference), keeping drives alive and converting more consistently.

football_factors.name: Defensive Resistance
football_factors.reason: PHI's defense is slightly more stingy than KC's — allowing 0.028 fewer EPA per play and limiting opponent scoring opportunities.

football_factors.name: Pressure Matchup
football_factors.reason: KC wins the pass rush vs. protection battle slightly (0.024 sack-rate edge) — a mismatch that can collapse key third-down drives.
